title: No Return
notes: Terminal Contact defeat. There is deliberately no Horizon fallback.

lines.text: The monitor clips. Not loudly. Perfectly.
You knew the term before you opened it. The fault repeats the warning now without words, using the body that agreed as its meter.
The sentence has no return value.
Perhaps a man is dying somewhere ordinary and has built this entire field in the interval between one heartbeat and the next.
Perhaps there is no somewhere ordinary left, and the chunk has reached the part of the carrier that believed it was a man.
The recording cannot distinguish them. Neither can you.
No Horizon opens under the page. Nothing lets you walk the loss into another ending.
